situation (example wording): "Compare robbery in Florida, Texas, and New York since 1990", "anti-Asian hate crimes in New York vs California" (a state name that is also a city's name, named beside only states).
what the app does today: P28 asks which New York (the state or New York City) for a single place. P196 (on the reader branch, not yet on dev) reads a city named beside other places as that city's police, with no ask.
proposed behavior: When every other place named in the question is a state, a name that is also a state's name is the state, with no ask. "New York" beside only states means New York State, not New York City. A single place on its own still asks (P28). A city named beside other places that are not all states still follows P196, and Washington keeps P238. A place the question names as a city, county or police department keeps that meaning.
why: Jeff 2026-11-24 (through the coordinator): a state name beside only states is the state, no ask; New York beside only states is New York State. PR 317's code already does this; this row writes it down.
